phases.name: Assessment & Documentation
phases.subtitle: Full inspection of every system before any wrenching. Know exactly what you have before committing to anything.

phases.name: Frame
phases.subtitle: Choose and prepare the frame. Everything else assembles onto this foundation.

phases.name: Drivetrain
phases.subtitle: Transmission, transfer case, and axles — rebuilt and ready while everything is accessible.

phases.name: Engine
phases.subtitle: Assess engine condition, decide rebuild depth, execute. Tune for reliable running.

phases.name: Brakes
phases.subtitle: Complete brake system rebuild. Non-negotiable before the car moves under its own power.

phases.name: Suspension & Steering
phases.subtitle: Install lift kit and sort steering. Makes the car driveable and correct.

phases.name: Fuel System
phases.subtitle: Tank, lines, carb — all fresh. Must be right before any extended running.

phases.name: Cooling System
phases.subtitle: Pressure test, hoses, electric fan installation. Engine cannot run reliably without this.

phases.name: Electrical
phases.subtitle: Full harness inspection, fix bodge repairs, ground straps. Make all circuits trustworthy.

phases.name: Body & Assembly
phases.subtitle: Tub rust treatment, bed repair, then assemble the car back together.

phases.name: Commissioning
phases.subtitle: First start, break-in, systems check, initial drive. The car becomes a car again.

assess-engine.name: Engine visual inspection
assess-engine.notes: Do this BEFORE any start attempt. What you find here determines next steps.
steps: Check oil level and condition — color, consistency, smell, metal flakes
Look for external leaks: rear main seal, valve cover, oil pan, front seal
Check coolant in radiator — level, color, any oil contamination (milky = head gasket concern)
Inspect all hoses and belts visually
Look for obvious damage: cracks, broken mounts, damaged wiring
Note anything unusual before attempting to start

compression-test.name: Compression test — AMC 258
compression-test.notes: Results determine whether engine needs full rebuild or just tuning. This is the decision gate for Phase 4 depth.
steps: Disable ignition (pull coil wire)
Remove all 6 spark plugs
Thread compression gauge into cylinder 1
Crank engine 4–5 times, record reading
Repeat for all 6 cylinders
Expected: 150–170 PSI per cylinder. Variation >15% between cylinders = concern.
Low across all = rings. Low on adjacent cylinders = head gasket. Low on one = valve issue.

inspect-primary-frame.name: Inspect primary frame — rust assessment
inspect-primary-frame.notes: Be ruthless. Do not underestimate rust. This decision determines whether to use this frame or the spare.
steps: Clean frame rails with wire brush to reveal actual metal condition
Probe suspected areas with screwdriver — soft = structural rust
Check body mount cups (all 8) — top and bottom surface
Inspect rear frame extension welds (CJ8-specific)
Check front crossmember at spring perch welds
Check frame rails at all spring hangers
Measure rail wall thickness with ultrasonic thickness gauge if available
Document every area of concern with photos

inspect-spare-frame.name: Inspect spare CJ8 frame — rust assessment
inspect-spare-frame.notes: Run parallel to primary frame inspection. Both results compared in choose-frame task.
steps: Same inspection as primary frame — wire brush, probe, document
Inventory what is attached: brake lines, fuel lines, any brackets
Assess brake and fuel lines — reusable or replace?
Check rear extension welds and body mount cups

choose-frame.name: Choose primary build frame
choose-frame.notes: Bring photos to a Claude Code session to help evaluate if unsure. This is the most important decision of the project.
steps: Compare inspection results side by side
Identify which frame has less structural rust at critical points (body mounts, spring perches, rear extension)
Make the call — document in decisions.ts
The rejected frame becomes a parts donor (hardware, brackets, lines)

inspect-tub.name: Inspect tub — floor and body panels
inspect-tub.notes: Any rust-through in floor or body mounts requires welding — mark for shop.
steps: Remove any mats or coverings from floor
Inspect floor from inside and underneath — probe soft spots
Check lower sides (rocker area) for rust-through
Inspect firewall — especially lower corners
Check body mount plates from inside — these are load-bearing
Document all rust-through areas — these are welding jobs

inspect-bed.name: Inspect pickup bed — floor and sides
inspect-bed.notes: Bed rust is confirmed — this task determines the scope of the repair.
steps: Remove any debris from bed
Inspect floor from above and underneath
Probe all soft areas
Check bed walls, corners, and tailgate
Assess whether patch panels or full floor replacement is needed

inspect-front-axle.name: Inspect Dana 30 front axle
inspect-front-axle.notes: Car is on stands — good access.
steps: Check diff fluid level and condition
Rotate axle shaft and check for U-joint roughness or play
Check outer stub axle for play (grab and rock)
Inspect pinion seal for leaks
Check housing for cracks or damage

inspect-rear-axle.name: Inspect Dana 44 rear axle
inspect-rear-axle.notes: Confirm this is a Dana 44 (look for axle tube diameter and casting number).
steps: Check diff fluid level and condition
Rotate axle shaft and check for U-joint roughness or play
Check axle shaft end play (grab and pull in/out)
Inspect pinion seal and axle seals for leaks
Look for any housing damage

confirm-gear-ratio.name: Confirm front/rear gear ratio match
confirm-gear-ratio.notes: Critical — mismatched ratios damage the transfer case in 4WD. The previous owner who swapped in the Dana 44 may or may not have matched ratios.
steps: Mark rear driveshaft and axle yoke
Rotate rear wheel one full turn, count driveshaft rotations — that is the ratio
Repeat for front axle
Ratios must match within 0.1 for 4WD to work properly
If mismatch: bring to Claude Code session to plan resolution

inspect-transfer-case.name: Inspect Dana 300 transfer case
inspect-transfer-case.notes: Noise and hard shifting already known. This confirms the extent and guides rebuild scope.
steps: Check fluid level and condition
Attempt to shift through all positions (may be stiff — do not force)
Listen for noise in neutral
Check output seals for leaks
Note which positions are accessible and which are stuck

inspect-transmission.name: Inspect T4 transmission
inspect-transmission.notes: New clutch and mounts on hand. Transmission internals may be fine — inspect before assuming rebuild needed.
steps: Check fluid level and condition
Shift through all 4 gears — note any stiffness or skipping
Check for leaks at input shaft seal, output shaft seal, shift tower
Check transmission mounts (new mounts are on hand)

inspect-brake-lines.name: Inspect brake lines and hoses
inspect-brake-lines.notes: Assume all rubber components need replacement. Steel lines: assess individually.
steps: Trace every brake line from master cylinder to each wheel
Look for rust, kinks, soft spots, or weeping
Check flexible hoses at each axle — squeeze and look for cracking
Inspect master cylinder for external leaks
Note: all rubber hoses are 30+ years old and should be replaced regardless

inspect-wiring-harness.name: Inspect wiring harness and grounds
inspect-wiring-harness.notes: Document all bodge repairs — each is a task. Assessment only; no power until wiring is cleared.
steps: Trace main harness — look for brittle insulation, melted spots, splices
Photograph all visible bodge repairs
Check battery positive and negative cables — replace if corroded
Locate all ground straps (body-to-frame, engine-to-firewall, battery) and inspect
Do NOT power up yet — assess first

inspect-tires.name: Inspect tires — age and condition check
inspect-tires.notes: Brand new but 8 years in Israeli sun. Most likely: replace. Confirm with DOT date.
steps: Find DOT date code on each tire sidewall (last 4 digits = week/year of manufacture)
Inspect sidewalls for cracking, checking, or ozone deterioration
Flex each sidewall — cracking under flex = unsafe
If manufacture date > 6 years ago AND sidewall cracking present = replace
If structurally sound despite age = inspect again after mounting and report back

frame-rust-treatment.name: Frame rust removal and treatment
frame-rust-treatment.notes: This is the most important prep step. A properly treated frame lasts another 30 years. Do not rush.
steps: Wire brush or sand blast all frame surfaces
Apply rust converter (POR-15 or equivalent) to any rust-pitted areas
Allow to cure fully
Apply chassis paint or epoxy primer to all surfaces
Pay special attention to inside of frame rails (use wand applicator)

frame-weld-repairs.name: Frame structural repairs (shop — welding)
frame-weld-repairs.notes: Shop job — owner does not weld. Cost estimate is rough — depends on inspection findings.
steps: Identify all areas needing weld repair from inspection
Take to trusted welding shop
Repair cracks, re-weld body mount cups if needed, patch any rust-through
Have shop confirm structural integrity before returning

frame-body-mount-inspection.name: Replace body mount hardware
frame-body-mount-inspection.notes: Old rubber mounts are certain to be deteriorated. Replace as part of frame prep.
steps: Replace all 8 body mount rubbers (30+ years old — all cracked)
Replace body mount bolts if corroded
Clean and chase all mount threads

strip-spare-frame.name: Strip spare frame — salvage usable parts
strip-spare-frame.notes: Only if spare frame is not chosen as primary build frame.
steps: Remove all usable hardware: bolts, brackets, lines
Assess brake and fuel lines from spare frame — reuse if in good condition
Catalogue salvaged parts
Set aside unusable frame for disposal

rebuild-transfer-case.name: Rebuild Dana 300 transfer case
rebuild-transfer-case.notes: Noise + hard shifting = rebuild required. Do while drivetrain is accessible.
steps: Drop transfer case from vehicle
Disassemble — inspect input shaft bearing, shift forks, chain, seals
Replace: input shaft bearing, all seals, shift fork if worn
Inspect chain — replace if stretched
Reassemble with new gaskets
Fill with fresh 75W-90 gear oil

service-front-diff.name: Service Dana 30 front differential
service-front-diff.notes: Minimal service unless inspection reveals bearing issues.
steps: Drain and inspect old fluid — metal particles = bearing wear
Replace pinion seal
Replace axle seals
Refill with fresh 75W-90 GL-5

service-rear-diff.name: Service Dana 44 rear differential
steps: Drain and inspect old fluid
Replace pinion seal and axle seals
Refill with fresh 75W-90 GL-5

replace-front-ujoint.name: Replace front axle U-joints
replace-front-ujoint.notes: Replace regardless of apparent condition — cheap insurance while accessible.
steps: Remove front driveshaft
Press out U-joints
Install new Spicer 1310 U-joints
Grease and reinstall

replace-rear-ujoint.name: Replace rear driveshaft U-joints
steps: Remove rear driveshaft
Press out U-joints
Install new Spicer 1310 U-joints
Grease and reinstall

replace-trans-mounts.name: Install new transmission and transfer case mounts

parts.name: Transfer case / gear mount (new — on hand)

steps: Support trans/TC with jack
Remove old mounts
Install new mounts

install-clutch.name: Install new clutch kit
install-clutch.notes: Clutch kit on hand. Do this while transmission is out for inspection.
steps: Remove transmission
Inspect flywheel — resurface if scored
Install new clutch disc and pressure plate
Install new pilot bearing and throw-out bearing
Reinstall transmission
Adjust clutch free play

engine-oil-inspection.name: Engine oil inspection and change
engine-oil-inspection.notes: What comes out tells you a lot about engine health. Cut the filter open with a rag and look.
steps: Drain old oil — inspect for metal particles, water (milky), or fuel contamination
Remove and cut open old oil filter — inspect for metal debris
Install new filter
Fill with fresh 10W-30

replace-engine-mounts.name: Install new engine mounts
replace-engine-mounts.notes: Parts on hand. Old mounts are 30+ years old and certainly deteriorated.
steps: Support engine from below with jack and block of wood
Remove old mounts (likely seized bolts — penetrating oil first)
Install new mounts
Torque to spec

carb-rebuild.name: Rebuild Carter YF carburetor

parts.name: New seal and cap for Carter (on hand)

carb-rebuild.notes: All parts on hand. After 8 years, a full rebuild is mandatory — gummed passages certain.
steps: Remove carb from engine
Disassemble completely — jets, needle/seat, accelerator pump, power valve
Clean all metal parts in carb cleaner
Blow out all passages with compressed air
Install all new rubber parts from rebuild kit
Install new seal and cap (on hand)
Reassemble and set float level
Reinstall and adjust mixture screws and idle speed

tune-up-ignition.name: Ignition tune-up
tune-up-ignition.notes: All original ignition components are 30+ years old. Replace everything.
steps: Replace all 6 spark plugs (Champion RN11YC, gap 0.035")
Replace distributor cap and rotor
Replace plug wires
Set base timing to 8° BTDC with timing light
Check and adjust vacuum advance

replace-exhaust-manifold.name: Inspect / replace exhaust manifold
replace-exhaust-manifold.notes: AMC 258 exhaust manifold cracks are nearly universal. Inspect first — if cracked, must replace.
steps: Inspect manifold carefully for cracks — ports, collector, flanges
If cracked: order replacement (do NOT attempt to weld cast iron)
Remove old manifold (seized bolts likely — heat and penetrating oil)
Install new manifold with new gaskets
Torque to 23 ft-lb in sequence

engine-deep-rebuild.name: Engine internal rebuild (conditional)

parts.name: Engine rebuild kit (pistons, rings, bearings, gaskets)

engine-deep-rebuild.notes: CONDITIONAL: only if compression test shows low/uneven compression. If compression is good, skip this and do tune-up only. This is the most expensive task on the plan.
steps: Pull engine from vehicle
Send block to machine shop for boring/honing
Replace: pistons, rings, bearings (mains + rods), gaskets
Inspect and recondition head
Rebuild and reinstall

replace-brake-lines.name: Replace brake lines
replace-brake-lines.notes: Lines from the spare frame may be reusable — compare condition. If spare frame lines are clean, use them.
steps: Remove all old brake lines
Install pre-bent replacement steel line kit
Or: fabricate lines with brake line tube and flare tool
Connect all fittings — do not over-tighten

replace-wheel-cylinders.name: Replace all wheel cylinders
replace-wheel-cylinders.notes: After 8 years sitting, all wheel cylinders are seized or corroded. Replace all four.
steps: Remove all 4 drums
Replace all 4 wheel cylinders
Inspect drums for scoring and measure — replace if beyond spec
Install new brake shoes front and rear
Reinstall drums

replace-brake-drums-shoes.name: Inspect and replace brake drums
replace-brake-drums-shoes.notes: May not need replacement — measure first.
steps: Measure drum inside diameter with brake drum micrometer
Replace any drum beyond maximum diameter stamped on drum
Clean drum contact surface

install-brake-booster.name: Install new brake booster
install-brake-booster.notes: Brake booster on hand. Need new master cylinder.
steps: Remove old brake booster and master cylinder as assembly
Install new brake booster
Bench bleed new master cylinder
Install master cylinder on booster
Connect vacuum line to intake manifold

install-proportioning-valve.name: Install new proportioning valve
steps: Remove old proportioning valve
Install new valve in correct orientation
Connect all brake lines

bleed-brakes.name: Bleed complete brake system
bleed-brakes.notes: Last brake task. Do not move the car until pedal is firm.
steps: Fill master cylinder with fresh DOT 4
Bleed: right rear → left rear → right front → left front (furthest to closest)
Use vacuum bleeder or two-person method
Check for firm pedal — no sponginess
Test brake booster: press pedal with engine off, start engine — pedal should drop slightly

inspect-spring-mounts.name: Inspect spring mounts and shackles before lift install
inspect-spring-mounts.notes: Installing new springs on compromised mounts defeats the purpose.
steps: Inspect front and rear spring hangers for cracks or rust
Check spring shackles for wear or damage
Replace any compromised hardware before installing new kit

install-lift-kit.name: Install Rubicon Express 2.5" lift kit

parts.name: Rubicon Express 2.5" lift kit — leafs + shocks (on hand)
New U-bolts (check kit — may be included)

install-lift-kit.notes: Kit is on hand. At 2.5" no SYE needed, but check brake line length after install.
steps: Support vehicle — remove weight from axles
Remove old leaf springs and shocks (all 4 corners)
Install new Rubicon Express leaf springs front and rear
Install new U-bolts
Install new Rubicon Express shocks
Check driveshaft angles at new ride height
Check brake line length — may need extensions at new height

replace-drag-link.name: Replace drag link
steps: Remove old drag link
Install new drag link
Check toe — adjust at tie rod if needed

install-steering-damper.name: Install new steering damper
install-steering-damper.notes: On hand. Straightforward after drag link is installed.
steps: Remove old damper
Install new damper in correct orientation
Check for full steering lock-to-lock clearance

inspect-steering-box.name: Inspect steering box and tie rod ends
inspect-steering-box.notes: Box replacement or rebuild is a significant cost — adjust first if possible.
steps: Check steering wheel free play — more than 2" = box worn
Check tie rod ends for play
Inspect steering shaft U-joint
Adjust steering box if play is borderline (there is an adjustment screw)

replace-tie-rod-ends.name: Replace tie rod ends (if worn)
replace-tie-rod-ends.notes: After tie rod end replacement, get a proper toe alignment.
steps: Count turns to remove old ends (for reinstall reference)
Install new ends same number of turns
Set toe: 1/8" toe-in — verify with string or alignment shop

inspect-fuel-tank.name: Inspect and clean fuel tank
inspect-fuel-tank.notes: Condition unknown — must inspect. Best case: clean and seal. Worst case: replace.
steps: Remove tank
Drain any remaining fuel (8-year-old fuel — dispose properly)
Inspect interior with light for rust and sediment
If surface rust only: clean with tank sealer (POR-15 tank kit or similar)
If heavily rusted or holed: replace tank

clean-fuel-tank.name: Clean and seal fuel tank
clean-fuel-tank.notes: Only if inspection shows rust but not holes.
steps: Rinse tank with fuel system cleaner
Shake with gravel to loosen rust
Rinse thoroughly
Apply POR-15 tank sealer or equivalent
Allow full cure before reinstalling

replace-fuel-lines.name: Replace all fuel lines
replace-fuel-lines.notes: All rubber fuel lines are 30+ years old and ethanol has attacked the rubber. Replace entirely.
steps: Remove all rubber fuel lines (tank to carb, return line)
Install new ethanol-resistant fuel line throughout
Replace fuel filter
Check all fittings for leaks

install-electric-fan.name: Install electric cooling fan

parts.name: Electric fan (on hand — came with radiator)

install-electric-fan.notes: Fan has been waiting since the radiator was upgraded. Good addition for Israeli summers.
steps: Mount fan to radiator
Wire to switched power with inline fuse
Install thermostat switch in radiator (if using automatic control)
Test operation

pressure-test-radiator.name: Pressure test radiator and cooling system
pressure-test-radiator.notes: Prior crack + repair is a risk. Pressure test BEFORE attempting any start.
steps: Install radiator pressure tester
Pump to 15 PSI
Hold for 10 minutes — any drop = leak
Inspect radiator repair area carefully
If leak: repair or replace radiator before any startup attempt

replace-cooling-hoses.name: Replace all cooling hoses
replace-cooling-hoses.notes: All hoses are 30+ years old. Replace entirely before any startup attempt.
steps: Replace upper radiator hose
Replace lower radiator hose
Replace all heater hoses
Replace bypass hose
Refill with fresh 50/50 coolant

replace-thermostat.name: Replace thermostat
replace-thermostat.notes: $10 part, easy job, must be done.
steps: Drain coolant below thermostat level
Remove housing, extract old thermostat
Install new 195°F thermostat with new gasket
Torque housing bolts

replace-water-pump.name: Replace water pump
replace-water-pump.notes: After 8 years sitting, impeller may have corroded off shaft. Replace as standard practice.
steps: Drain coolant
Remove fan, fan belt, and pulley
Remove old pump
Install new pump with new gasket
Reinstall pulley and belt

check-ground-straps.name: Inspect and replace ground straps
check-ground-straps.notes: Bad grounds cause 80% of mysterious electrical problems. Do this first before chasing anything.
steps: Locate all ground straps: battery(-) to chassis, engine to firewall, body to frame
Inspect all attach points for corrosion — clean with wire brush
Replace any strap that is corroded, frayed, or broken
Ensure all attach surfaces are bare metal (remove paint at attachment)

test-all-circuits.name: Test all electrical circuits
test-all-circuits.notes: Systematic circuit-by-circuit test. Document what works and what doesn't.
steps: Install charged battery
Test: lights (head, tail, brake, turn)
Test: horn, wipers, gauges
Test: ignition circuit, starter
Note any non-functioning circuits — each is a task

repair-wiring-harness.name: Repair bodge wiring and brittle harness sections
repair-wiring-harness.notes: Repair known issues. If extensive, consider a full harness replacement (Painless Performance — major cost).
steps: Address each bodge repair found in inspection
Replace any section with brittle or cracked insulation
Use proper connectors — no bare twisted splices
Wrap repaired sections with self-amalgamating tape or loom

test-charging-system.name: Test alternator and charging system
test-charging-system.notes: Test before buying anything — may be fine.
steps: With engine running: measure voltage at battery terminals
Should be 13.8–14.5V — anything less = alternator or voltage regulator issue
Check alternator output at the B+ terminal
Replace alternator if not charging correctly

tub-rust-treatment.name: Tub rust treatment and repair
tub-rust-treatment.notes: Scope unknown until inspection. Weld repairs are shop work.
steps: Any rust-through: weld repair (shop job)
Surface rust: wire brush, rust converter, primer
Paint floor and lower panels with rubberized undercoat
Paint visible panels with chassis black or body color

bed-rust-repair.name: Pickup bed rust repair
bed-rust-repair.notes: CJ8 bed floors are hard to find as replacement panels — repair in place is the usual approach.
steps: Identify all rust-through areas — welding shop job
Wire brush all remaining rust
Apply rust converter to pitted areas
Spray with bed liner or rubberized coating

install-body-mounts.name: Mount tub to frame
install-body-mounts.notes: Body mount kit covered in frame-body-mount-inspection task.
steps: Install new body mount rubbers on frame
Lower tub onto frame — align all mount holes
Install body mount bolts — torque to spec

mount-tires.name: Mount tires and install wheels
mount-tires.notes: If 8-year-old tires pass inspection: ₪150 for mounting. If they fail: ₪2,000+ for replacements.
steps: Mount tires on wheels (tire shop)
Install on vehicle — torque lug nuts to spec (90 ft-lb)
Check tire pressure (32 PSI start — adjust to preference)

final-assembly.name: Final assembly and pre-start checklist
final-assembly.notes: Checklist before first start — all fluids in, all lines connected, all grounds clean.
steps: Reconnect all electrical connectors
Reconnect fuel and brake lines
Reconnect driveshafts
Install hood, doors, and any body panels removed
Verify all fluid levels before startup

pre-start-checklist.name: Pre-start safety checklist
pre-start-checklist.notes: Do not skip this. Check everything before cranking.
steps: Oil level — full
Coolant level — full
All fuel lines connected, no smell of fuel
All brake lines connected
Battery connected, grounds clean
No visible leaks from any system
Fire extinguisher nearby
Have someone present for first start

first-start.name: First start — 8 years
first-start.notes: The moment 8 years of work pays off. Have a camera ready.
steps: Crank without spark (pull coil wire) to build oil pressure — 5 seconds
Restore ignition — start engine
Immediately check: oil pressure gauge, any leaks, exhaust color
Let idle — watch temperature gauge closely
If temp rises quickly — shut down, investigate
Target: warm up to operating temp, check for stable idle

break-in-drive.name: Initial drive and systems test
break-in-drive.notes: Stay close to home for first drive.
steps: Short initial drive — 5km, varied speed, no highway
Test brakes: controlled stop from 30 km/h
Test steering: figure-8 in parking lot
Test all 4WD positions: 2H → 4H → 4L → back
Return and inspect everything: leaks, noises, temperatures

post-drive-inspection.name: Post first-drive inspection
post-drive-inspection.notes: The first drive always reveals something. Document it all.
steps: Check all fluid levels — oil, coolant, trans, diff (F+R), TC
Look under the car for any new leaks
Listen for any noises that were not present before drive
Check brake pad/shoe clearance (if drums feel hot)
Bring findings to Claude Code session — update plan

decisions.rationale: Owner preference for stock-ish build focused on mechanical reliability. The 258 is a strong, proven unit when properly rebuilt. Swapping adds complexity, cost, and fabrication work inconsistent with the build goals.
Owner wants a reliable daily driver with light off-road capability. Not a rock crawler or show build. This keeps the scope manageable and the budget focused on mechanical integrity.
Kit is already on hand. 2.5" is appropriate for mild off-road use — good clearance without requiring driveline angle correction. No SYE needed at this lift height.

decisions.summary: Two frames — choose the better one
decisions.rationale: Primary frame has concerning rust. A matching spare CJ8 frame (with brake and fuel lines) is available. This is unusual luck — use it. The better frame becomes the build foundation.

decisions.summary: Full DIY — owner has welding equipment and workshop
decisions.rationale: Owner confirmed: has tools, workshop, equipment, and welding knowledge. Nothing goes to a shop unless specifically chosen to.
Dana 44 is significantly stronger than the AMC 20. No axle shaft cracking risk. No reason to downgrade. Only action: confirm gear ratio matches Dana 30 front, service the diff.
